name: Name a numeral to 20
description: Student can say the number name when shown a numeral from 0 to 20.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown the card 14, the student says 'fourteen'.
commonError: Student reverses teen numbers (reads 14 as 'forty'), or does not recognise 0 as zero.
checkpointTask: Show numeral cards 0 to 20 in random order. Ask the student to name each.

name: Make a collection to match a number
description: Student can collect the right number of objects when given a number name or numeral up to 20.
exampleOfSuccess: Hearing 'nine', the student counts out 9 paintbrushes.
commonError: Student grabs a handful without counting, or stops at the wrong number.
checkpointTask: Name several numbers to 20. Ask the student to collect that many objects each time.

name: Write or form numerals
description: Student can write or form numerals from 0 to 20.
exampleOfSuccess: Asked to write 'seven', the student writes 7 the right way around.
commonError: Student reverses digits (writes 7 or 3 backwards) or forms teen numbers in the wrong order.
checkpointTask: Say several numbers to 20. Ask the student to write each numeral.

name: Order numbers to 20
description: Student can put numbers from 0 to 20 in order.
exampleOfSuccess: Given mixed cards 0 to 10, the student lays them out in order from 0 to 10.
commonError: Student orders by where there is space, or skips or repeats a number.
checkpointTask: Give the student a set of number cards to 20. Ask them to put them in order.

name: Say one more and one less
description: Student can say the number that is one more and one less than a given number to 20.
exampleOfSuccess: Asked one more than 12, the student says 13; one less than 12, says 11.
commonError: Student counts from one each time, or cannot go backwards for 'one less'.
checkpointTask: Name several numbers to 20. Ask for one more and one less for each.

name: Use ordinal numbers
description: Student can use ordinal words (first, second, third, fourth, fifth) to say position in a sequence.
exampleOfSuccess: Lining up toys, the student names which is first, third and fifth.
commonError: Student uses counting numbers (one, two) instead of ordinal words, or miscounts the position.
checkpointTask: Line up five objects. Ask the student which is first, second, third, fourth and fifth.

name: Subitise collections to 3
description: Student can say how many are in a small collection of 1 to 3 with a quick look, without counting.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown three dots briefly, the student says 'three' straight away.
commonError: Student counts the dots one by one rather than recognising the amount at a glance.
checkpointTask: Flash dot cards of 1, 2 and 3 briefly. Ask the student how many, allowing only a quick look.

name: Subitise to 5
description: Student can subitise collections up to 5 in familiar arrangements such as dice or dot patterns.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown a dice face of five, the student says 'five' without counting.
commonError: Student can subitise to 3 but counts for 4 and 5.
checkpointTask: Flash dice or dot patterns to 5. Ask the student how many with only a quick look.

name: Subitise different arrangements
description: Student can subitise to 5 when the objects are arranged in different, non-standard ways.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown four dots in a line and four in a square, the student says 'four' for both.
commonError: Student only recognises the standard dice patterns and counts any other arrangement.
checkpointTask: Flash collections of 4 and 5 in unusual arrangements. Ask the student how many each.

name: Compare small collections by subitising
description: Student can compare two small collections by subitising and say which has more.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown 3 dots and 5 dots, the student says the second has more without counting.
commonError: Student says the more spread out group has more, regardless of how many.
checkpointTask: Show pairs of small dot collections. Ask the student which has more, with a quick look.

name: Count a collection to 20
description: Student can count a collection of up to 20 objects, touching or moving each one once.
exampleOfSuccess: Counting a pile of 15 counters, the student touches each once and reaches 15.
commonError: Student skips an object or counts one twice, so the count is wrong.
checkpointTask: Give the student a collection of up to 20 objects. Ask them to count how many.

name: Know the last number tells how many
description: Student can say that the last number they counted tells how many there are altogether.
exampleOfSuccess: After counting to 12, asked 'how many?', the student says 12 without recounting.
commonError: Student recounts from the start when asked how many, not knowing the last number is the total.
checkpointTask: After the student counts a collection, ask 'so how many are there?' and watch whether they recount.

name: Count stays the same when rearranged
description: Student can recognise that the number in a collection stays the same when the objects are moved around.
exampleOfSuccess: After counting 8 counters, the student sees them spread out and says it is still 8 without recounting.
commonError: Student thinks spreading the objects out makes more, or bunching them makes fewer.
checkpointTask: Count a collection with the student, rearrange it, and ask how many now.

name: Compare collections by counting
description: Student can compare two collections by counting and say which has more and which has fewer.
exampleOfSuccess: Counting 7 red and 9 blue, the student says there are more blue.
commonError: Student compares by which pile looks bigger rather than by counting.
checkpointTask: Give two collections of similar size. Ask the student to find which has more by counting.

name: Count out a number for a purpose
description: Student can count out a needed number of items for a task.
exampleOfSuccess: Asked to get enough cups for 6 children, the student counts out 6 cups.
commonError: Student takes too many or too few, or does not connect the count to the purpose.
checkpointTask: Set a purpose (one cup each for a group). Ask the student to count out exactly enough.

name: Explain or show their counting
description: Student can explain or demonstrate how they counted to know how many.
exampleOfSuccess: The student shows they touched each counter once and that the last number was the total.
commonError: Student gives an answer but cannot show or say how they worked it out.
checkpointTask: After a count, ask the student to show you how they counted and how they know that is how many.
reviewNotes: Serves the 'explain or demonstrate reasoning' clause of the descriptor.

name: Split a collection into two parts
description: Student can partition a collection of up to 10 into two parts.
exampleOfSuccess: Given 6 counters, the student splits them into a group of 4 and a group of 2.
commonError: Student leaves some counters out of both parts, or the parts do not make the whole.
checkpointTask: Give the student up to 10 counters. Ask them to break them into two groups.

name: Combine two parts to find the whole
description: Student can put two parts together and say how many there are altogether.
exampleOfSuccess: With a part of 3 and a part of 4, the student combines them and says 7.
commonError: Student counts only one part, or recounts incorrectly when combining.
checkpointTask: Give the student two small groups. Ask how many there are altogether.

name: Recognise a number on a ten-frame
description: Student can recognise how many are shown on a ten-frame and describe the parts.
exampleOfSuccess: Shown 7 on a ten-frame, the student says 'seven, that is 5 and 2 more'.
commonError: Student counts every box including empty ones, or counts the filled ones one by one each time.
checkpointTask: Show numbers to 10 on a ten-frame. Ask how many and how they can tell.

name: Show different ways to make a number
description: Student can partition the same number up to 10 in more than one way.
exampleOfSuccess: For 5, the student shows 4 and 1, then 3 and 2.
commonError: Student gives the same split twice with the parts swapped and counts it as different.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to show two different ways to make 5 using counters.

name: Say the part-part-whole relationship
description: Student can say both parts and the whole for a partitioned collection.
exampleOfSuccess: Splitting 8 into 5 and 3, the student says '5 and 3 make 8'.
commonError: Student names the parts but not the whole, or the whole but not the parts.
checkpointTask: Partition a collection with the student. Ask them to say the two parts and the whole.

name: Show an adding-to story with materials
description: Student can use objects to act out an adding-to situation from a story.
exampleOfSuccess: For 'there were 3 ducks and 2 more came', the student sets out 3 then adds 2.
commonError: Student shows only one quantity, or does not add the second group.
checkpointTask: Tell a short adding story to 10. Ask the student to show it with counters.

name: Show a taking-away story with materials
description: Student can use objects to act out a taking-away situation from a story.
exampleOfSuccess: For '5 apples and 2 were eaten', the student sets out 5 and removes 2.
commonError: Student removes the wrong number, or adds instead of taking away.
checkpointTask: Tell a short taking-away story to 10. Ask the student to show it with counters.

name: Find how many after adding
description: Student can count to find how many there are after more are added.
exampleOfSuccess: After adding 2 to 3 ducks, the student counts and says 5 altogether.
commonError: Student counts only the added group, or starts the count from zero on the last object.
checkpointTask: Pose adding situations to 10. Ask the student to show it and say how many now.

name: Find how many are left after taking away
description: Student can count to find how many are left after some are removed.
exampleOfSuccess: After removing 2 from 5, the student counts the rest and says 3 are left.
commonError: Student counts the removed group as the answer, or miscounts what remains.
checkpointTask: Pose taking-away situations to 10. Ask the student to show it and say how many are left.

name: Represent a simple money or quantifying situation
description: Student can use materials to represent a simple quantifying or whole-coin money situation.
exampleOfSuccess: For 'buy a 2 dollar toy with coins', the student counts out 2 one-dollar coins.
commonError: Student treats the coins as plain counters with no value, or cannot match coins to the amount.
checkpointTask: Pose a simple whole-dollar buying situation. Ask the student to show it with play money.

name: Share a collection equally
description: Student can share a small collection equally between people or groups, giving one at a time.
exampleOfSuccess: Sharing 6 counters between 2 toys, the student deals one each in turn, giving 3 each.
commonError: Student shares unevenly, or gives all to one before the other.
checkpointTask: Give the student counters and two toys or plates. Ask them to share equally.

name: Make equal groups
description: Student can make equal groups from a collection.
exampleOfSuccess: Asked to make groups of 2 from 8 counters, the student makes 4 pairs.
commonError: Student makes groups of different sizes.
checkpointTask: Give the student counters. Ask them to make equal groups of two or of five.

name: Check that shares are equal
description: Student can check that each share or group has the same number.
exampleOfSuccess: After sharing, the student counts each plate to check they all have 3.
commonError: Student assumes the shares are equal without checking, even when they are not.
checkpointTask: After the student shares a collection, ask them to check that each group is the same.

name: Notice when it will not share evenly
description: Student can notice when a collection cannot be shared equally and that some are left over.
exampleOfSuccess: Sharing 7 between 2, the student gives 3 each and says one is left over.
commonError: Student forces an even share by ignoring or hiding the extra.
checkpointTask: Pose a share that does not work out evenly (7 between 2). Ask what happens to the extra.
